gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Woodgod stands tall, its lowercase nearly touching the capitals. Noto Sans Buginese is the modern counterpart, leaving its curves unjoined like a chalk arc, so the heading carries the vintage command and the sans keeps the text light.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid is a modern, professional sans-serif with generous gaps between its curve ends and stems. Woodgod then takes the vintage, commanding role on top, and its tall lowercase stands out against the body's high-set x-height.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Large and open, with curves that stop short instead of closing in, this body reads contemporary and clear. Noto Sans Chorasmian sits under Woodgod's vintage swagger, and the heading's tall lowercase gives the page a strong first impression.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Vintage muscle meets modern polish. Woodgod commands attention with tall lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals, while Noto Sans Coptic does the quieter work of a sans-serif, its middle zone dominating the line with open, uncrowded shapes.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Woodgod's lowercase rises almost to capital height, giving it a vintage, commanding presence. But Noto Sans Cuneiform goes the other way, a clean sans-serif whose e opens up and whose rounded forms look swollen like inflated glass beads.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Noto Sans Duployan reads contemporary and clean, with oversized counters and a wide opening in the a. Over a full page of text, Noto Sans Duployan stays light and breathable, while Woodgod's vintage heading holds the top.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Commanding is how Woodgod comes across, with a vintage weight and lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals. And Noto Sans Elbasan reads smoothly through longer text, its large lowercase and open terminals that never pinch shut keeping the sans-serif body easy going.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Woodgod brings a vintage, commanding display voice, with tall lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals. And if that heading were made small or the Noto Sans Ethiopic body made large, the sturdy sans would start to crowd the display's character.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Vintage swagger on top, modern clarity below, with Woodgod's tall lowercase leading and Noto Sans Georgian's open curves following. Longer text stays smooth and clean, its sans-serif letters never feeling cramped.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Old-world command, then a modern hush. Woodgod suits a big, bold size for its tall lowercase, while Noto Sans Grantha is fine smaller, its flattened bowls reading smoothly with no closed-up snags.
